nate (oncall): Heads up — seeing intermittent packet loss between pods in gpu-pool-a (us-east-2). Rough numbers: about 0.5-3% packet loss on some east-west flows, p99 latency spikes. Appears only on overlay (encap) path; host-level underlay looks clean. Started ~03:20 UTC yesterday after the nic-driver rollout. Filing here to coordinate.

maria (sre): When did the rollout run and which nodes are affected? Any kernel or firmware changes included in that batch? :eyes:

aj (infra): Rolled nic-driver v1.4.2 to node-group gpu-us-east-2 at 2026-03-16T03:14Z. No firmware bump in the same run. I did see a small uptick in tx-queue drops in pmon after the rollout. Pulling host counters now.

infra-bot: ROLLOUT: nic-driver v1.4.2 deployed to group/gpu-us-east-2 at 2026-03-16T03:14:27Z (trigger: infra/driver-canal)

aj (infra): quick tcpdump from pod-host (canary-02) during a failing ping window:
```
14:12:03.123456 IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 54321, frag 0) 10.40.5.12 > 10.40.6.7: UDP, length 1400
14:12:03.123459 IP 10.40.5.12.58012 > 10.40.6.7.9000: UDP, length 1200
14:12:03.223401 IP 10.40.6.7 > 10.40.5.12: ICMP echo reply, id 1, seq 42, length 64
14:12:03.323501 IP 10.40.5.12 > 10.40.6.7: ICMP echo request, id 1, seq 43, length 64
14:12:03.323550 IP 10.40.6.7 > 10.40.5.12: IP, bad checksum  (udp checksum 0x0)
```
Noting some 'bad checksum' lines on encap decode, but host NIC offloads can make tcpdump lie.

hua: Can we check checksum offload/GRO/GSO states? We saw similar with GENEVE where offloads + large segments caused inner packet drops. `ethtool -k` on the veth/nic and `sysctl` for net.core.* might reveal it.

nate (oncall): `ethtool -k eth0` shows: tx-checksumming: on, rx-checksumming: on, gso: on, gro: on. I'll toggle gro/gso off on a single canary host and re-run ping/iperf to see if loss stops.

aj (infra): Observed qdisc/ifb drops spike when pod counts > ~800 connections. Also ran iperf3 between two pods: with MTU 9000 it's fine, with MTU 1400 throughput collapses and retransmits increase — possible fragmentation or encap MTU path issue.

maria (sre): Can we run a controlled probe capturing both outer/inner headers and collect /proc/net/snmp and ethtool counters during the window? If we can reproduce on canary, we can either toggle offloads or rollback driver. Schedule a 10min test window.

aj (infra): Putting together a tiny runbook/script to toggle offloads and run probes. Script (draft):
```
#!/bin/bash
# toggle offloads, run ping/iperf, collect counters
for IF in eth0 ; do
  ethtool -K $IF gro off gso off tso off
done
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc=1
ping -c 50 10.40.6.7 > /tmp/ping_canary.log
iperf3 -c 10.40.6.7 -t 20 > /tmp/iperf_canary.log
cat /proc/net/dev > /tmp/dev_canary.log
```

nate (oncall): Plan: run the script on 2 canary nodes in gpu-pool-a during a 10min window, gather tcpdumps (outer+inner decode), ethtool counters, and dmesg. If loss goes away with GRO/GSO off, we'll roll that toggle to the rest of the pool and schedule a driver rollback test. Pausing autoscaler for canary time. :thumbsup:

hua: Also capture kernel ring buffer for mlx5: `dmesg -T | tail -n 80`. I saw intermittent 'mlx5_core: ERR: ...' on one host earlier; could be related.

infra-bot: ACTION CREATED: NET-345 Investigate intermittent overlay packet drops (assignee: nate (oncall), priority: high, due: 2026-03-17)

maria (sre): If any customer-facing batch fails, escalate to #incidents. Keep updates short here — we need clear pass/fail for the canary test.

nate (oncall): Starting canary at 2026-03-16T14:20Z. Will post results in ~15m with collected artifacts and next steps.
